How soon must it be registered?","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-R01"]},"answer":{"text":"Within ten days.","fact_ids":["sec05-F01"]},"rationale":{"text":"Newcomers file inside ten days, and titles prove ownership before plates issue.","fact_ids":["sec05-R01"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec05-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Getting your car registered","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-F02","sec05-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Registration, plates and title","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-F02","sec05-F03"]},{"text":"Who files and when","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-F02","sec05-F03"]},{"text":"Renewal deadlines","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-F02","sec05-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Before a car is driven in Florida, the owner has paperwork to complete, and this lesson walks through it. Every car owned here needs Florida registration, plates and a title. Newcomers have a short deadline to register a car they bring with them. Titles and plates are issued at service centers, and who files the paperwork depends on whether you bought from a dealer or a private seller. Finally, registrations must be renewed by set dates that depend on the type of vehicle, and renewal opens ninety days before that date.","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-F02","sec05-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"What every owner needs","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Florida registration, plates and title","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-R01"]},{"text":"Newcomers register within ten days","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-R01"]},{"text":"Insurance and title prove the claim","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"An owned car needs Florida registration, plates and a title. Someone who moves here and brings a car must register it within ten days. Insurance and the title together prove the owner's claim. A used car coming from another state has its vehicle identification number verified, except for light trailers and new vehicles. In a worked example, Robin moves to Florida with a car registered elsewhere. Robin registers it within ten days, shows insurance and the title, and has the VIN verified, which completes the newcomer steps.","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":35,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Titles and plates","fact_ids":["sec05-F02","sec05-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Service centers title and plate by weight and type","fact_ids":["sec05-F02","sec05-R01"]},{"text":"Dealers file for buyers; private buyers file themselves","fact_ids":["sec05-F02","sec05-R01"]},{"text":"Titles come before plates","fact_ids":["sec05-F02","sec05-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Service centers issue titles and plates according to the vehicle's weight and type. Plates must stay current, and the registration papers ride in the car. When you buy from a dealer, the dealer files the paperwork for you. When you buy from a private seller, you file it yourself. In every case, the title comes before the plates. Drivers who hold a license from another state also get licensed here first. So the order to remember is ownership first, through the title, and then the plate that lets the car be driven. Dealer or private, the title still comes first.","fact_ids":["sec05-F02","sec05-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"When registration expires","fact_ids":["sec05-F03","sec05-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Most cars: yearly or every two years, at birthday midnight","fact_ids":["sec05-F03","sec05-R02"]},{"text":"Mobile homes and semis: December thirty-first","fact_ids":["sec05-F03","sec05-R02"]},{"text":"Fleets: June thirtieth; renewals open ninety days early","fact_ids":["sec05-F03","sec05-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Registrations run for one or two years and expire at midnight on the owner's birthday. Mobile homes and semis run to December thirty-first instead, and fleets run to June thirtieth. Renewal opens ninety days early for all of them, and insurance is checked again at renewal. So an ordinary car owner renews around their birthday, a fleet renews at midyear, and mobile homes and semis renew at the end of the year. Insurance has to be current at that point too, since renewal rechecks it. Mark your renewal date and check your insurance before it arrives.","fact_ids":["sec05-F03","sec05-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u01-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Title before plate","fact_ids":["sec05-R01","sec05-F01","sec05-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"The title proves ownership","fact_ids":["sec05-R01","sec05-F01","sec05-F02"]},{"text":"Plates come after the title","fact_ids":["sec05-R01","sec05-F01","sec05-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Some people think the plate is the first step, since it is the visible part of registration. The handbook puts the title first: titles prove ownership before plates are issued. A second trap is the newcomer deadline. It is ten days, which is short, so a new resident should not wait until a license renewal or a birthday. Also remember that used out-of-state cars need a VIN check, with light trailers and new vehicles as the exceptions. Ownership, then plate, all within the deadline. Ten days is the number to hold onto.","fact_ids":["sec05-R01","sec05-F01","sec05-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the newcomer deadline","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"A car from another state","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-R01"]},{"text":"How soon must it be registered?","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a newcomer brings a car from another state. How soon must the car be registered in Florida? Pick your answer before going on. The answer is within ten days. Newcomers file within ten days, insurance and the title prove ownership, and titles come before plates are issued. A used car from another state also has its vehicle identification number verified, unless it is a light trailer or a new vehicle, which are the listed exceptions. Those two exceptions are the only ones the handbook lists for the VIN check, so every other used car from another state is checked.","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Registration recap","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-F02","sec05-F03","sec05-R01","sec05-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Ten days for newcomers","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-F02","sec05-F03","sec05-R01","sec05-R02"]},{"text":"Birthday midnight, ninety days early","fact_ids":["sec05-F01","sec05-F02","sec05-F03","sec05-R01","sec05-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"To recap, Florida-owned cars need registration, plates and a title, and newcomers register within ten days. equipment, and some equipment is not allowed at all. This lesson covers both lists. The required list includes dual brakes, several kinds of lamps with set distances, signals, a horn, mirrors, wipers and plain safety glass. The banned list includes front-facing red and blue lamps, extra-lamp trios, sirens and bells, loud or smoking mufflers and stickers on the glass. Low beams must light one hundred fifty ahead and be seen at one thousand. High beams must light four hundred fifty and also be seen at one thousand. Tail lamps must be seen at one thousand, brake lamps at three hundred in daylight, and plate lamps at fifty. Signals are listed at five hundred, and horns and mirrors at two hundred. Dual brakes, wipers, plain safety glass, tint limits and minimum tread depth complete the required list. Front-facing red lamps and blue lamps are not allowed, and neither is a trio of extra lamps. Sirens and bells are banned. A muffler that is loud or smokes past fifty feet is banned, and so are stickers on the glass. All of these items cause a car to fail inspection. In a worked example, Kim wants to add a forward-facing blue light to the car. Blue lamps are on the banned list, so Kim must not add it, and a siren or bell would be just as unacceptable. A television the driver can see is banned, and so is wearing a headset while driving. Both distract the driver. The owner's manual answers questions specific to your car. Airbags are also covered: they assist the seat belt but never replace it. Kim's second idea, a small television on the dashboard where the driver can see it, is therefore banned too. The common thread is that the driver's eyes, ears and protection must stay focused on safe driving. When a question is about the cabin, think about what the driver sees and hears.","fact_ids":["sec05-F06","sec05-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u02-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Airbags do not replace belts","fact_ids":["sec05-R05","sec05-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Airbags only assist","fact_ids":["sec05-R05","sec05-F06"]},{"text":"Belts are still required","fact_ids":["sec05-R05","sec05-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"The trap is believing that an airbag reduces the need for a seat belt. The handbook says airbags assist belts and never replace them. A related trap is thinking that a screen is fine as long as it is small. Any television the driver can see is banned, whatever its size, and worn headsets are banned as well. So the protective equipment and the driver's attention both have firm rules: buckle the belt every time, treat the airbag as an extra, and keep screens out of the driver's view. Keep the belt on and the screens out of the driver sight line.","fact_ids":["sec05-R05","sec05-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u02-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the beam distances","fact_ids":["sec05-R03","sec05-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Low beams versus high beams","fact_ids":["sec05-R03","sec05-F04"]},{"text":"How far ahead does each light?","fact_ids":["sec05-R03","sec05-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: how far ahead must low beams light the road, and how far must high beams light it? Tail lamps are also seen at one thousand, brake lamps at three hundred by day and plate lamps at fifty, so keep each distance matched to its lamp when a question changes one of them. Low beams light the shorter distance, high beams the longer one, and both are seen from the same distance of one thousand.","fact_ids":["sec05-R03","sec05-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u02-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Equipment recap","fact_ids":["sec05-F04","sec05-F05","sec05-F06","sec05-R03","sec05-R04","sec05-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Required lamps with set distances","fact_ids":["sec05-F04","sec05-F05","sec05-F06","sec05-R03","sec05-R04","sec05-R05"]},{"text":"No red or blue up front","fact_ids":["sec05-F04","sec05-F05","sec05-F06","sec05-R03","sec05-R04","sec05-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"To recap, required equipment includes dual brakes, low beams lighting one hundred fifty and high beams four hundred fifty, both seen at one thousand, tail lamps seen at one thousand, brake lamps at three hundred by day, plate lamps at fifty, signals, horn, mirrors, wipers, plain safety glass, tint limits and tread depth. Front-red and blue lamps, extra-lamp trios, sirens, bells, loud or smoking mufflers and glass stickers are banned, as are driver-visible televisions and worn headsets, and airbags only assist belts.","fact_ids":["sec05-F04","sec05-F05","sec05-F06","sec05-R03","sec05-R04","sec05-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":33,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec05-u03","module_id":"sec05-m03","objective_ids":["sec05-u03"],"title":{"text":"Driver assistance systems","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-F08","sec05-F09"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Assistance systems help, but each has limits, and none replaces the driver's own checks.","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-F10"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Chris backs out of a driveway using only the backup camera.","fact_ids":["sec05-F10","sec05-R08"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Backup cameras never replace mirrors and head turns.","fact_ids":["sec05-F10","sec05-R08"]},"result":{"text":"Chris should also check the mirrors and turn to look before backing.","fact_ids":["sec05-R08"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a blind-spot warning system will steer you away from a crash.","fact_ids":["sec05-R06"]},"correction":{"text":"Warning helpers only alert; it is acting helpers that brake or steer back.","fact_ids":["sec05-R06","sec05-F07","sec05-F08"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Warners warn, actors act.","fact_ids":["sec05-R06"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Does a lane-departure warning system steer the car back into its lane?","fact_ids":["sec05-R06","sec05-F07"]},"answer":{"text":"No, warning-only helpers alert without ever acting.","fact_ids":["sec05-F07"]},"rationale":{"text":"Warning helpers only alert, while acting helpers brake and steer back.","fact_ids":["sec05-R06"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec05-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Help from the car","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-F08","sec05-F09","sec05-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Warning-only helpers","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-F08","sec05-F09","sec05-F10"]},{"text":"Acting helpers","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-F08","sec05-F09","sec05-F10"]},{"text":"What never replaces the driver","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-F08","sec05-F09","sec05-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"Many cars now carry systems that help the driver, and this lesson sorts them by what they actually do. Some only warn you: they flag a blind spot, a closing gap, lane drift or cross traffic behind you, but they never take action. Others act: they brake for frontal and pedestrian crashes or nudge a drifting car back. Further aids brake while reversing, keep a gap, center the car or keep it in its lane. And some features call for help, switch headlights or show a camera view, which never replaces your own checks. We will take the groups one at a time.","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-F08","sec05-F09","sec05-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Warning-only helpers","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-R06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Blind spots, closing gaps, lane drift","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-R06"]},{"text":"Reverse cross traffic","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-R06"]},{"text":"They warn but never act","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-R06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Warning-only helpers alert the driver to a blind spot, a gap closing ahead, the car drifting from its lane, or cross traffic while reversing. They never act on their own. That means the driver still has to brake or steer. A lane-departure warning, for example, tells you the car is drifting, but it does not move the car back. Treat these systems as an extra set of eyes that speaks up, not as a system that will take over. The decision and the action remain with the driver every time. The driver still makes every move.","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-R06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Acting helpers","fact_ids":["sec05-F08","sec05-R06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Brake for frontal and pedestrian crashes","fact_ids":["sec05-F08","sec05-R06"]},{"text":"Nudge back a drifting lane change","fact_ids":["sec05-F08","sec05-R06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Acting helpers go a step further than warnings. They brake to help prevent frontal crashes and crashes with pedestrians, and they nudge a car back when it drifts during a lane change. So the key difference between the two groups is action: warning helpers only alert, while acting helpers brake or steer back. Knowing which kind your car has matters, because a driver who believes a warning system will act could wait too long. Check the owner's manual for your own car's features. Warning helpers alert; acting helpers act.","fact_ids":["sec05-F08","sec05-R06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u03-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Automated controls and other aids","fact_ids":["sec05-F09","sec05-F10","sec05-R07","sec05-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Reverse braking, adaptive cruise, centering, keeping","fact_ids":["sec05-F09","sec05-F10","sec05-R07","sec05-R08"]},{"text":"Lane keeping can combine control actions","fact_ids":["sec05-F09","sec05-F10","sec05-R07","sec05-R08"]},{"text":"Crash callers, auto beams, backup cameras","fact_ids":["sec05-F09","sec05-F10","sec05-R07","sec05-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Driving aids perform different control functions. Reverse braking guards you while backing, adaptive cruise keeps a spacing gap, lane centering holds the middle of the lane, and lane keeping can combine steering, braking or acceleration to correct lane drift. Other features help in different ways: crash callers summon rescuers, and automatic beams switch with traffic. Backup cameras show the area behind you, but they never replace mirrors and head turns. In a worked example, Chris backs out using only the camera. The handbook says Chris must still check the mirrors and turn to look.","fact_ids":["sec05-F09","sec05-F10","sec05-R07","sec05-R08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":35,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u03-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Warnings are not actions","fact_ids":["sec05-R06","sec05-R07","sec05-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Warning helpers only alert","fact_ids":["sec05-R06","sec05-R07","sec05-R08"]},{"text":"Cameras never replace mirrors and looks","fact_ids":["sec05-R06","sec05-R07","sec05-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"The trap is trusting a system to do more than it does. A blind-spot or lane-drift warning only alerts you; it will not brake or steer. Only acting helpers brake for frontal and pedestrian crashes or nudge a drifting car back. Lane keeping may combine steering with braking or acceleration to return the vehicle to its lane. And a backup camera, however clear, never replaces checking mirrors and turning your head. So keep driving as if the systems were not there, and treat every alert or camera image as extra information on top of your own checks. The systems add information, not judgment.","fact_ids":["sec05-R06","sec05-R07","sec05-R08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u03-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the warning system","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-R06"]},"lines":[{"text":"A lane-departure warning","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-R06"]},{"text":"Does it steer you back?","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-R06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a car has a lane-departure warning system. Does that system steer the car back into its lane? Choose your answer before continuing. The answer is no. Warning-only helpers flag blind spots, closing gaps, lane drift and reverse cross traffic without ever acting. Steering back belongs to acting helpers and to lane keeping, which corrects straying wheels, so a driver who has only a warning system must make the correction personally. Lane keeping and acting helpers are the ones that can move the car back, while a warning-only system leaves the steering to you.","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-R06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u03-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Assistance systems recap","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-F08","sec05-F09","sec05-F10","sec05-R06","sec05-R07","sec05-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Warners warn, actors act","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-F08","sec05-F09","sec05-F10","sec05-R06","sec05-R07","sec05-R08"]},{"text":"Look for yourself","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-F08","sec05-F09","sec05-F10","sec05-R06","sec05-R07","sec05-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"To recap, warning-only helpers flag blind spots, closing gaps, lane drift and reverse cross traffic without ever acting. Acting helpers brake for frontal and pedestrian crashes and nudge back drifting lane changes.
